attributes.moa: Aminopenicillin beta-lactam; binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan cross-linking.

drugs.name: Cephalexin

attributes.moa: First-generation cephalosporin; inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins.

indications: Bone infections due to susceptible organisms
metabolism: Dose adjustment may be needed in renal impairment

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone

attributes.moa: Third-generation cephalosporin; inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis with broad gram-negative activity.

metabolism: Avoid calcium-containing IV solutions in neonates

drugs.name: Azithromycin

attributes.moa: Macrolide antibiotic; binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.

metabolism: Limited CYP3A4 inhibition compared with clarithromycin

drugs.name: Clarithromycin

attributes.moa: Macrolide antibiotic; binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.

indications: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis
metabolism: Renal dose adjustment may be needed

attributes.moa: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

drugs.name: Levofloxacin

attributes.moa: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

metabolism: Dose adjustment needed in renal impairment

drugs.name: Omeprazole

attributes.moa: Proton pump inhibitor; irreversibly inhibits the gastric parietal cell H/K ATPase.
attributes.half_life: About 0.5 to 1 hour; acid suppression lasts longer

adrs: Vitamin B12 deficiency with prolonged use

drugs.name: Pantoprazole

attributes.moa: Proton pump inhibitor; irreversibly inhibits the gastric parietal cell H/K ATPase.
attributes.half_life: About 1 hour; acid suppression lasts longer

indications: Stress ulcer prophylaxis in selected patients
adrs: Fracture risk signal with prolonged use
metabolism: Primarily CYP2C19 metabolism with contribution from CYP3A4

attributes.moa: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; reduces hepatic cholesterol synthesis and increases LDL receptor activity.
attributes.half_life: About 14 hours; active metabolites last longer

drugs.name: Simvastatin

attributes.moa: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor prodrug; reduces cholesterol synthesis and increases LDL clearance.
attributes.half_life: About 2 hours for active beta-hydroxyacid metabolite

metabolism: Lactone prodrug converted to active metabolite
High interaction sensitivity with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors

attributes.moa: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; reduces cholesterol synthesis and increases LDL receptor activity.

drugs.name: Lisinopril

attributes.moa: ACE inhibitor; reduces angiotensin II formation, aldosterone secretion, and bradykinin degradation.

metabolism: Dose adjustment needed in renal impairment

drugs.name: Enalapril

attributes.moa: ACE inhibitor prodrug; active enalaprilat reduces angiotensin II formation and aldosterone secretion.

metabolism: Dose adjustment needed in renal impairment

drugs.name: Metoprolol

attributes.moa: Beta-1 selective adrenergic blocker; lowers heart rate, contractility, and AV nodal conduction.

indications: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
metabolism: Poor metabolizers may have increased exposure

attributes.moa: Nonselective beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic blocker; reduces sympathetic cardiac effects.

drugs.name: Warfarin

attributes.moa: Vitamin K antagonist; inhibits VKORC1 and reduces activation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.

metabolism: CYP2C9 metabolism for more potent S-warfarin
CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 contribute to R-warfarin metabolism

drugs.name: Apixaban

attributes.moa: Direct oral anticoagulant; selectively inhibits factor Xa.

indications: Venous thromboembolism prevention after hip or knee replacement
adrs: Spinal or epidural hematoma risk with neuraxial procedures

drugs.name: Clopidogrel

attributes.moa: P2Y12 ADP receptor antagonist prodrug; inhibits platelet activation and aggregation.
attributes.half_life: About 6 hours for parent drug; active metabolite is short lived

metabolism: CYP2C19 inhibitors can reduce antiplatelet activity
Irreversibly inhibits platelets for their lifespan

interactions.description: Clarithromycin can strongly inhibit CYP3A4 and markedly increase simvastatin exposure, increasing myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk.

details.management: Avoid combination; hold simvastatin or use a non-CYP3A4 statin when appropriate.

interactions.description: Clarithromycin can increase atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk through CYP3A4 inhibition.

details.management: Avoid when possible or monitor closely; consider temporary statin interruption.

interactions.description: Clarithromycin may increase apixaban exposure through combined CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition.

details.management: Assess bleeding risk and follow product-label guidance.

interactions.description: Macrolides can increase anticoagulant effect in warfarin-treated patients, increasing bleeding risk.

details.mechanism: Altered metabolism and gut flora effects
details.management: Check INR more frequently during and after therapy.

interactions.description: Azithromycin has reported INR elevation risk in warfarin-treated patients despite less CYP inhibition than clarithromycin.

details.management: Monitor INR and bleeding signs.

interactions.description: Ciprofloxacin can increase INR and bleeding risk in patients taking warfarin.

details.mechanism: CYP inhibition and gut flora effects
details.management: Monitor INR closely; adjust warfarin if needed.

interactions.description: Levofloxacin can increase INR and bleeding risk in patients taking warfarin.

details.management: Monitor INR closely.

interactions.description: Omeprazole can reduce clopidogrel antiplatelet activity by inhibiting CYP2C19 activation.

details.management: Avoid omeprazole when possible; consider alternatives such as pantoprazole when clinically appropriate.

interactions.description: Pantoprazole has a less pronounced effect on clopidogrel activity than omeprazole but still exercises the PPI comparison card.

details.management: Often preferred over omeprazole when a PPI is needed with clopidogrel.

interactions.description: Combining anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk.

details.management: Use only with clear indication and monitor bleeding closely.

interactions.description: Combining apixaban with antiplatelet therapy increases bleeding risk.

details.management: Use the shortest appropriate duration when combination therapy is indicated.

interactions.description: Concurrent therapeutic anticoagulants generally duplicate anticoagulation and substantially increase bleeding risk.

details.management: Do not overlap except under a specific transition protocol.

interactions.description: Fluoroquinolone and statin coadministration has a myopathy signal and ciprofloxacin may add interaction risk.

details.management: Counsel on muscle pain and weakness.

interactions.description: Ciprofloxacin can inhibit CYP1A2 and may increase exposure to some beta blockers such as propranolol.

details.management: Monitor for bradycardia or hypotension.

interactions.description: Combining beta blockers duplicates beta blockade and increases risk of bradycardia, hypotension, and heart block.

details.management: Avoid routine combination.

interactions.description: Combining ACE inhibitors duplicates RAAS blockade and increases hypotension, renal impairment, and hyperkalemia risk.

details.management: Avoid routine combination.

interactions.description: No major direct interaction is expected; included as a low-severity comparator card.

details.mechanism: No major direct CYP or pharmacodynamic overlap
details.management: Routine monitoring.

interactions.description: No major direct interaction is expected; included as a low-severity comparator card.

details.mechanism: No major direct CYP or pharmacodynamic overlap
details.management: Routine monitoring.

interactions.description: Some antibiotics can alter INR control in warfarin-treated patients.

details.mechanism: Possible gut flora and illness effects
details.management: Monitor INR when clinically warranted.

interactions.description: Cephalosporins may potentiate anticoagulant effect in some warfarin-treated patients.

details.management: Monitor INR and bleeding signs.

interactions.description: Omeprazole may affect warfarin exposure or INR control in some patients.

details.management: Monitor INR after starting or stopping therapy.

interactions.description: Both drugs can prolong QT interval, increasing additive arrhythmia risk.

details.management: Avoid combination in high-risk patients when alternatives exist.

interactions.description: Both drugs can prolong QT interval, increasing additive arrhythmia risk.

details.management: Avoid combination in high-risk patients when alternatives exist.

interactions.description: Combining fluoroquinolones duplicates therapy and toxicity risk without a routine therapeutic role.

details.management: Avoid routine combination.

interactions.description: Combining statins duplicates lipid-lowering therapy and increases myopathy risk.

details.management: Avoid routine combination.

details.management: Avoid routine combination.
